name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, a pine-covered hill station at about 1,500 m elevation known as the Scotland of the East. Colonial architecture, markets, lakes, and base for exploring Khasi Hills attractions.

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m (1,115 ft), plunging from the Sohra plateau edge near Cherrapunji into a turquoise pool. Famous for dramatic cliffs, legend of Ka Likai, and views of Bangladesh plains.
facts: Located near Sohra (Cherrapunji) in East Khasi Hills
Fed by plateau rainwater; strongest in monsoon
Plunge pool has distinctive green hue

name: Elephant Falls
description: Popular multi-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong in Upper Shillong area. Known locally as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew (three-step waterfall), set amid fern-covered rocks and easy access paths.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city center
Original Khasi name means three-step waterfall

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at approximately 1,965 m, about 10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, hills, and distant plains; sacred to Khasi people as abode of U Lei Shillong.
facts: Air Force radar station nearby; ID required
Best for sunset and clear-day views

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town and former wettest place on Earth on the southern Khasi Hills plateau in East Khasi Hills. Famous for extreme rainfall, waterfalls, living root bridges, caves, and views over Bangladesh plains.
facts: Base for waterfalls, caves and root bridges

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in Pynursla block of East Khasi Hills known as the cleanest village in Asia. Matrilineal Khasi community with 100% literacy, bamboo dustbins, living root bridges nearby, and border views.
facts: Awarded cleanest village in Asia (2003) and India (2005)
About 90 km from Shillong near Bangladesh border
Features skywalk and nearby root bridges

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village near Sohra, formed by guiding Ficus elastica roots across a stream. Requires a steep trek of thousands of steps from Tyrna; UNESCO-recognized bioengineering.
facts: Located in Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills
Part of living root bridge tradition of Khasi people

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village in East Khasi Hills, protected for centuries by Khasi tradition as the abode of the deity Labasa. Dense old-growth forest with unique flora and no removal of anything allowed.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong on Shillong-Sohra road
Home to rare plants and biodiversity
Visitors guided; nothing to be taken from forest

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall about 315 m high near Mawsmai village in East Khasi Hills, plunging over limestone cliffs in seven streams. Best in monsoon; offers views of Bangladesh plains.
facts: Also known as Seven Sisters or Mawsmai Falls
Illuminated by sunlight in clear weather

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra in East Khasi Hills, about 150 m long with stalactites, stalagmites and fossil impressions. Short, tourist-friendly exploration with lighting.
facts: Khasi name means Oath Stone Cave
Tourist path is short and managed

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Laitlum village in East Khasi Hills, about 25 km from Shillong. Steep grassy slopes drop into deep valleys with views of distant plains and villages.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum and research centre in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing cultures of Northeast Indian tribes across multiple galleries. Includes artifacts, traditional houses, skywalk, and educational facilities.
